step_title: Fire the object-injection POST to reach phpinfo()
prevented: Proved the deserialization primitive was real before switching to a Metasploit module, rather than trusting the version banner.

step_title: Confirm blind execution out-of-band with an ICMP ping
prevented: Confirmed a blind injection reached code execution before committing to a reverse shell.

step_title: Confirm with the advisory's own PoC
prevented: Confirmed the CVE applied to this target before hand-building an exploit.
Avoided building a TOCTOU exploit against a version outside the vulnerable range.
The CVE needs a layout bind-mount. No snap mount existed, so the scanner hit was a false positive.
Second scanner-flagged CVE ruled out on its kernel-module precondition rather than by firing it.
Established reactor state before touching it, so later changes could be attributed to the exploit.

step_title: Probe the HMI from inside the shell
prevented: Confirmed what was actually listening on 8081 before building a tunnel to it.
Distinguished a real privilege change from an endpoint that merely returned 200.

step_title: Try the VPN endpoint as a non-admin
prevented: Showed access control worked elsewhere, so the settings bypass was a real distinct bug.
Static decompilation and a live LDAP capture produced the same credential. Two methods, one answer.
Confirmed the host really was the domain PDC before building an attack path on that assumption.
RBCD needs the ability to add a computer account. Checked the quota before assuming the path was open.

step_title: Ask the service how it authenticates
prevented: Read the server's own description of its auth model instead of assuming an alg:none weakness.

step_title: Trigger a capture and download it
prevented: Opened his own capture first, so another user's exposed data was recognisable as such.
Ruled out the simplest unauthenticated foothold before moving to the web surface.
Learned the exact message fields the service trusted before crafting a malicious one.
Tested the obvious pattern first and got a 403, which is what justified trying double-encoding.
Confirmed the archive held a KeePass database before spending effort opening it.
Confirmed the recovered credential authenticated before spending an exploit attempt on it.
Confirmed the exact token structure from front-end code instead of assuming a generic pattern.
Confirmed the CA trust was genuinely unrestricted before signing a certificate claiming root.
Confirmed the signed certificate actually claimed the root principal before trying to use it.
